about: The openings of a well-known building as they are, wall by wall, in place of what the church rule gives (v2/data/scene/landmarks.py; facades.md rules 31 to 35; the owner's decision of 23 Nov 2026: 'look for images and aerial photos and figure it out'). One entry per ACT building id. datum: the altitude (m) its heights are measured from. A wall: at = a point (E, N; LUREF) on the wall's foot, the wall's left end as seen from outside; facing = the compass bearing its outside looks to; openings = [kind, x0, x1, z0, z1, head]: x in metres from `at` to the right as seen from outside, z in metres above the datum, kind one of lancet, traceried, belfry, oculus, rose, head one of pointed, round, flat (a round window has none); courses = string courses (z above the datum). A wall named here loses the rule's windows, courses and drawn buttresses; a wall not named keeps the rule. measured: capture = read off v1's aerial capture of the area flattened onto the wall (0.125 m a pixel, about half a metre sure); photo = counted and placed from the photographs named, by eye (about a metre sure); mirror = not seen from any source, set as the mirror of the other side, which the photographs show to be alike. Only what a source shows is entered: a part of a wall that no source shows keeps no opening.
